newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on fund selling.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on fund selling, centered in the March contract, traders said.
"Fund selling pressured wheat and late fund selling pressured soyoil," Kucha said. "No deliveries on the December was a little supportive."

E.D. & F. Man International sold eight million bushels of March and Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold four million bushels of March, traders said. Merrill Lynch Futures bought four million bushels of March, they said.
Fundamentals were little changed with tight nearby stocks and firm basis markets underpinning prices.
The strong basis values and dwindling supply of wheat in the marketing channels drew further attention to the posting of no deliveries Friday on the December contract.
There was talk that one to two million bushels would be posted Friday on the December contract. Friday was first notice day for deliveries on the CBOT December contracts.
The market was underpinned by news Turkey will be in the market December 10 for 200,000 tonnes of wheat and there are hopes the U.S. will land a good portion of the business.
Wheat closed 4-1/2 to 6-3/4 cents lower, with December down 4-1/2 at $3.96 per bushel.
Also, there was news overnight that Turkey bought 25,000 tonnes of wheat from Argentina but there were reports Morocco passed on a tender for 20,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat.
Pressure over the wheat market also came from a lighter-then-expected number for wheat in USDA's weekly export sales report.
USDA Friday said U.S. net exports of wheat during the week ended November 21 totaled 231,400 tonnes, below expectations for 350,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, below the 12,605 traded Wednesay, according to the CBOT.
Wheat options trade was likewise slow with Dean Witter Reynolds a noted buyer of 500 July $3.40 calls at 20 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 2,500 contracts, about the same as the 2,518 traded Wednesday.
